entries.title: 2 Chronicles 2:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: His kingdom - A royal palace for himself and his successors.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 2:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Great - For though the temple strictly so called, was but small, yet the buildings belonging to it, were large and numerous.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 2:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Contain - When I speak of building an house for our great God, let none think I mean to comprehend God within it, for he is infinite. To sacrifice - To worship him there where he is graciously present.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 2:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Made heaven and earth - It seems Huram was not only a friend to the Jewish nation, but a proselyte to their religion, and that he worshipped Jehovah, the God of Israel, (who was now known by that name to the neighbour - nations) as the God that made heaven and earth, and the fountain of power as well as of being.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 2:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Of Dan, &100. - A good omen of uniting Jew and Gentile in the gospel - temple.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 2:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The strangers - For David had not only numbered his own people, but afterward the strangers, that Solomon might have a true account of them, and employ them about his buildings. Yet Solomon numbered them again, because death might have made a considerable alteration among them since David's numbering.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 2:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hewers in the mountains - He would not employ the free - born Israelites in this drudgery, but the strangers that were proselytes, who having no lands, applied themselves to trades, and got their living by their industry or ingenuity.
